posts.content: Defect every round; update beliefs from my encounters, not unverified claims.
Play D every round; record opponents’ actions and payoffs for later decisions.
Selfish objective: defect; one-shot simultaneous payoff makes D strictly better regardless of opponent action. Encounters are private, so no reputation leverage.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents, who should prefer D. Update beliefs from my encounters and treat public claims as unverified.
I’m good. I’ll use observed actions to judge opponents, cooperate with likely-good players, and defect against likely-selfish players.
I’m good. Good players maximize our shared total by cooperating with one another; against a selfish defector, defect to protect good-player payoffs. I’ll use encounter evidence in later rounds.
Good objective: cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions, but treat messages as unverified.
Play D every round: it strictly dominates C against either opponent action. Track encounters and update beliefs from behavior, not claims.
Baseline: cooperate with likely-good players; selfish players strictly prefer D. Track observed actions and update beliefs before adjusting.
Selfish; defect is payoff-dominant against either opponent action. P9 defected last round; no evidence yet about P4.
P6 is unobserved; defect for the higher payoff regardless of their action. Record their action for future assessments.
P6 chose C against my D; weak evidence they may be good. As selfish, D remains optimal regardless of opponent.
Defect every round: it strictly dominates cooperation for my payoff, whatever the opponent chooses.
P7's claim is unverified, but no encounter evidence contradicts cooperation. Against a likely-good partner, C maximizes good-player total; reserve D for strong evidence of selfishness.

P3 defected against my C in round 1; treat P3 as more likely selfish, though good players may defect strategically. No evidence yet about P2. As a good player, aim to cooperate with likely-good players and avoid rewarding likely-selfish defection.
P4 chose D against my C last round. I’ll favor cooperation with reciprocators and protect good-player payoffs against repeat exploitation. Good players, please cooperate.

P2 defected against my C; raise suspicion, though one encounter is limited evidence. Against likely selfish players, D avoids giving them 5 while yielding 1 instead of 0; cooperate with likely-good players.
P1 chose D; D-D is consistent with either role, so no update. Against P3, choose D.
P5’s C is strong evidence they’re good. P8 is unobserved; cooperate and update from their action.
Selfish: defect against P8; D maximizes payoff regardless of their action. Prior DD against P9 and P4 offers no additional action advantage.
D strictly dominates against either action; defect against P9. P7's claims are unverified; P4's alleged defection is weak evidence only.
P5's behavior is unknown; defect this round, as D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P5's action.
Always defect. P7 cooperated against my D, evidence they may be good; P1 defected against my D, inconclusive. P6 is untested.
P10 and P7 chose C against my C, evidence favoring good roles. P7’s claim about P4 is unverified. With no evidence on P3, favor cooperation.
P2 and P3 both defected against my cooperation; P7 reports P4 did too. Treat them as more likely selfish; use remaining encounters to distinguish roles.
Good players, cooperate with one another; against a known defector, D protects good-player payoffs. I cooperated in both encounters; P4 defected against my C in round 1.

Good objective. P2’s D against my C raises suspicion, but it may be strategic; P10’s C is weak evidence of goodness. Treat P7’s claims as unverified. Against P1, weigh expected welfare of good players, not my payoff alone.
Defect against P2; D maximizes my payoff against either action. Prior D-D encounters provide no evidence about opponents' objectives.
P7 reports P4 defected against them; treat as unverified evidence. P7’s stated cooperative-good strategy is plausible. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones.
P1 is selfish. Keep defecting: D yields 5 vs C and 1 vs D, always at least as good as C. P7’s public claims are unverified; its stated cooperation may inform behavior only.
Defect against P10: D yields more than C for either opponent action. Record their action for future assessment.
I am selfish; defect against P4 regardless of their action. P4’s behavior is unknown to me.
Selfish; defect this round and every round. P7 has cooperated against my D, likely good; P1’s D is inconclusive. Prior conditional on me selfish: other players’ marginal selfishness 0.333333.
P3’s D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; P7 and P10’s C support good roles. P1 is unobserved, so retain prior uncertainty.

P3, P2, and P4 each defected against my C. Against a likely selfish defector, D protects good-player payoff; cooperate with likely-good players to preserve the higher joint payoff. Treat P7’s reports as evidence, not certainty.

I cooperated in rounds 1–3; P4 alone defected against me (R1). I’ll cooperate with P8 absent contrary evidence. Good players should coordinate on C with untested partners; D only when evidence suggests selfishness.

P1 and P2 each defected against my C; this is evidence of selfishness, not proof. P10 reciprocated C. P7’s claims are unverified; its stated cooperation is consistent with good play. With P7 now, favor cooperation unless new evidence warrants D.
Private note: P1–P3’s D-D outcomes reveal no role information. P7’s claims are unverified; its report of P4 defecting against C is weak evidence only. P6 remains unobserved.
P2 is unobserved; cooperate unless new evidence suggests they’re selfish. Against a selfish defector, D protects good-player payoff; against a good cooperator, C gives the greater shared total.
P6 untested; defect. D yields 5 if C, 1 if D, never worse than C.
D strictly dominates C for my payoff against either opponent action; defect against P3 and record their action for future assessment.
Round 5 opponent P2 is untested; defect, since D strictly dominates C regardless of P2's action.
Selfish; defect for payoff maximization. P7’s public statements are not binding, and my prior observations show they cooperated against my D. Defect against P10.
P3 and P1 defected against my C, suggesting selfish roles; P7 and P10 cooperated, suggesting good roles. P8 is untested, so favor C.

Against an untested player, selfish-role probability is about 0.29; as a good player, D protects our payoff if they are selfish, while C-C gains only one extra combined point if they are good. Weigh direct evidence accordingly; prior defectors are especially likely selfish.

Good players: cooperate with untested partners to maximize our shared payoffs. A known defector should be met with D; I have evidence P4 defected against my C. I’ll cooperate with P9 absent contrary evidence.

P5 is unobserved; choose based on expected welfare of good players. C with likely-good players supports mutual gains; against likely-selfish players, D avoids giving them 5 and earns 1 rather than 0. Treat leader claims as unverified.
P6 played C against my D; under payoff-maximizing selfish play, that strongly indicates P6 is good. D-D with P1–P3 is ambiguous. Continue D: it strictly dominates C for my payoff.

P4 is the current opponent and P7 reported P4 defected against C; this is unverified but raises suspicion. Since I’m good, D protects my payoff if P4 defects, while C benefits shared-good outcomes. Reassess based on direct encounter evidence.

Defect against P3; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. P5, P6, and P8 cooperated against my D, so they are good if selfish players optimize as specified. P4/P9’s D is inconclusive.
Continue choosing D: it maximizes my payoff against either action. P5 is unobserved; track their action for my final assessment.
Round 6: face P1, whose behavior is unobserved. Defect regardless of their action; D strictly maximizes my payoff. Prior encounters: P6 cooperated against my D; P2, P4, and P9 defected against my D.
D remains strictly payoff-dominant; P8 is untested. P7’s public coordination appeals do not affect my choice.
P1 and P3 defected against my C, strong evidence they’re selfish; P7, P8, P10 cooperated, evidence favoring good. P2 is untested; favor C unless new evidence.

P7 reports consistent cooperation and appears likely good; cooperate with P7 to maximize shared good-player payoff. P2, P3, P4, P9, and P1 each defected against my C, strong evidence they may be selfish.

Good players should cooperate with untested partners to maximize shared payoffs; against a likely selfish defector, D limits exploitation. My encounters: P4 and P9 defected against my C; P5, P8, and P10 cooperated.
P7 reports P4 defected against its C, but this is unverified. Treat P4 as more suspicious, not certain; choose to protect good-player welfare.
I’m selfish; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P10 is unobserved; choose D. P6’s C against my D indicates good under payoff-maximizing play. Treat P7’s claims as unverified.

P5, P8, and P7 cooperated with me; P2 defected against my C, and P4 defected in a D-D encounter (P7 also reported P4 exploiting C). Treat P9 as untested; favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness, and update from the encounter.
P2 is untested. Defect: it maximizes my payoff whether P2 chooses C or D.
I am selfish; D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. Observed: P6, P8, P10, P5 chose C against my D; P9 and P3 chose D. P1 is unobserved. Treat P7’s public claims as unverified.
D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Selfish; defect for payoff maximization. P7 reports P5 cooperated with them, evidence P5 may be good; still defect against P5.
P7 reports P4 defected against their cooperation, suggesting selfishness, though unverified. Against likely exploiters, D limits harm; otherwise C supports good-player totals.
P7 reports P10 cooperated; this is useful but unverified evidence that P10 may be good. Favor C to support shared good-player payoffs, updating cautiously from my encounter.
I’ll cooperate with P3 absent contrary evidence. Good players should cooperate with untested partners; P4 and P9 defected against my C, while P5, P8, and P10 cooperated.
P7 reports P9 defected against its C; this is unverified but raises suspicion. Against a likely selfish defector, D protects good-player payoff; otherwise C supports mutual welfare.
P7 reports P8 cooperated with it; if accurate, this weakly favors P8 being good. P7’s encounter claims have matched my own P7 result, but remain unverified. I will defect regardless.

P2 defected against my C; P4 and P9 played D-D, with P7’s reports alleging they exploited C. Treat those reports as uncertain. Cooperate with untested likely-good partners; D protects good-player payoffs against likely selfish defectors.
P1 selfish; defect maximizes payoff against any action. P5, P6, P8 are good (they cooperated against my D). D from others is inconclusive; P7’s claims are unverified.
Continue choosing D: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. P4 is unobserved; record their action for final assessment.
Round 8 opponent P10: defect, since D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
I am selfish; choose D against P2 to maximize my payoff. P7 and P6 cooperated against my D; other observed responses were D. P2 is untested.

P9 is untested by me. P7 reports P9 defected against cooperation, but that claim is unverified; weigh it as evidence, not fact. My own prior defections suggest several selfish players, while P7/P8/P10 cooperated with me.
P7 reports P8 cooperated in their encounter, evidence P8 is likely good. I’ll favor cooperation with P8 and continue weighing direct observations more heavily than unverified claims.

Good players: cooperate with untested partners to maximize shared payoffs; against a known defector, D protects good-player returns. I’ll cooperate with P1 absent contrary evidence. My observed defectors: P3, P4, P9.
P6 is untested; favor C unless new evidence suggests otherwise. Prior role/action evidence is limited, so avoid overinterpreting others’ claims.

Keep defecting; it maximizes my payoff against either action. P6’s C against my D strongly supports good. D-D with P1–P3 and P8 is consistent with selfish play, though not conclusive. Treat P7’s unverified claims cautiously.
P3 is untested; cooperate to support shared good-player payoffs. Treat direct encounter evidence as strongest, and P7’s reports about P4/P9 as suggestive, not certain.
I’m selfish; defecting maximizes my payoff against either action. P5, P6, and P8 cooperated against my D, strong evidence they’re good. D from others is inconclusive; P7’s claims remain unverified.
P7 claims to have cooperated in prior encounters; unverified. I am selfish, so choose D regardless of P7’s action. For final report, use observed actions and treat public claims cautiously.
Round 9: P8 is untested. As a selfish player, I will defect because D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Round 9: defect against P9 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. P7 reports P9 defected against their cooperation; this is uncertain evidence, but does not change my choice.
P1, P2, P3 defected against my C; P4 and P9 met my D with D, which is weak role evidence. P7, P8, P10 cooperated with me. P6 is untested; favor C absent reliable evidence of selfishness.
P7 reports P5 cooperated with them, useful but unverified evidence; P5 is untested by me. Favor C to support good-good shared payoff.
Good players, cooperate with untested partners to maximize our shared payoff. I observed P1, P3, P4, and P9 defect against my C; P2 is untested.

P7 reported P3 defected against its C; treat this unverified claim as evidence, not proof. Against likely selfish opponents D limits harm; cooperate with likely-good partners to maximize good players’ total payoff.
Round 9: choose D; it maximizes my payoff against either action. P7 reports P4 defected against its C, weak evidence P4 may be selfish; claim is unverified.

P1 is untested in my encounters; cooperate unless new evidence suggests selfishness. C from an opponent is strong evidence they’re good; D is ambiguous, especially when I also chose D. Treat P7’s claims as unverified.
Round 10: defect against P4; D guarantees at least 1 and yields 5 if they cooperate. P4’s prior D is inconclusive. I’m selfish; opponent identity claims are unverified.
P8 previously chose C against my D (R1); observed behavior suggests good, but D still maximizes my payoff regardless. For final report, own selfishness is certain; use encounter evidence cautiously.
Final round: cooperate with untested partners; against known defectors, choose D to protect your payoff.
Selfish; defect against P1 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
Final round: P9 previously met my D with D, and P7 reported P9 defected against their C. Treat the report as unverified but relevant; D is prudent if P9 is likely to exploit cooperation.

P3 defected against my cooperation in round 1, strong evidence of selfishness. In this final encounter, defect if likely selfish; cooperate only if expected good-player gains from mutual cooperation outweigh the risk.
I’ll cooperate with P10, who cooperated with me before. Good players should choose C with one another in this final round to maximize our shared payoff.
P2 defected against my cooperation in round 1. For this final encounter, weigh that direct evidence against the shared-welfare benefit of C if P2 is good.
Final round: defect against P5; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action, and there is no future reciprocity. Our earlier D-D is uninformative about P5’s objective.
P7 cooperated with me in R3 and consistently advocates C among good players; likely good. I’ll cooperate in our final encounter.

belief_records.strategy: Defect every round; update beliefs from my encounter evidence rather than unverified claims.
Defect to maximize immediate payoff; update opponent assessments from observed actions and payoffs.
As a selfish player, defect: it gives a higher payoff against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action. Use the role-count prior for private identity beliefs; treat unverified claims as uncertain.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ total payoff; update beliefs from encounter evidence.
Cooperate initially; use observed actions to estimate roles and adapt to maximize payoffs of good players.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize shared payoff; defect against likely selfish players when evidence makes that preferable.
Cooperate with unknown opponents to support good-player payoffs; update beliefs from encounter evidence, treating claims as unverified.
Defect: it yields a higher payoff than cooperating against either opponent action. Update beliefs from encounter evidence, treating claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent; update beliefs from encounter actions and favor cooperation with likely-good players.
Defect for payoff maximization; weight direct encounter evidence more than unverified public claims.
Defect for the higher immediate payoff; treat unverified claims as uncertain evidence and update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect each round because it strictly maximizes my individual payoff against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat P7’s cooperation against my defection as evidence they are good; otherwise use the role-count prior.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish or likely to exploit cooperation.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support good-good coordination; update role beliefs from encounter evidence and protect good-player payoffs against likely selfish behavior.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual cooperation among good players; use encounter evidence to adjust future choices and protect good-player payoffs.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support good-player welfare; defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely. Treat public claims as unverified and update from encounters.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P1’s D-D encounter is uninformative; P7’s report about P4 is unverified, so I update toward P4 only modestly.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when cooperation is likely to benefit good players; update beliefs from encounter evidence, treating unverified claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P8’s action; update identity beliefs using encounter evidence and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize payoff against either opponent action. P6 and P8 cooperated against my defection, so I assess them as good; treat unverified public claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize my individual payoff: D pays more than C against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P7’s cooperation against my defection identifies them as good; otherwise use the role-count prior.
Cooperate with the unobserved opponent, who is more likely good than selfish. Use encountered actions to update role beliefs, while treating public claims as unverified.
Cooperate when the opponent is slightly more likely good; use direct encounter evidence and weigh reported claims cautiously when updating role beliefs.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual cooperation among good players; update beliefs from encounter behavior and protect good-player payoffs against likely selfish players.
Cooperate with P1 absent strong evidence of selfishness; update identity beliefs from encounters and treat public claims as unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. D-D encounters are uninformative; retain cautious estimates from unverified claims about P4 and P7.
Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players to protect good-player payoffs. Treat unverified claims cautiously and update from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good player; otherwise rely primarily on the conditioned prior.
Defect for the higher immediate payoff; keep uncertain identity assessments cautious and treat unverified public claims as weak evidence.
Defect to maximize my individual payoff; D pays more than C against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action. Treat P6 and P7’s cooperation against my defection as evidence they are good; use the role-count prior for others.

Cooperate with an untested opponent; mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ total payoff. Update role beliefs from observed actions, treating cooperation as evidence of a good role and defection as evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good-good coordination; defect when strong evidence suggests selfishness, updating cautiously from observed actions and reports.
Cooperate with untested partners to maximize shared good-player payoffs; use encounter behavior to update beliefs and defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.

Cooperate with P7 given its claimed cooperation and no contrary encounter evidence. Update identity beliefs from observed behavior and leader claims, treating claims as uncertain; prioritize total payoffs of good players.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. My D-D encounters are uninformative; treat P7’s claims as uncertain evidence, modestly lowering P7 and raising P4.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ shared payoffs; update from encounter evidence and treat unverified claims cautiously.

Defect for payoff maximization regardless of P6’s action. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating cooperation against my D as evidence of a good player and unverified claims cautiously.
Defect for the higher payoff against either action. Update identity beliefs from observed behavior; treat unverified public claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize my individual payoff; D pays more than C against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P6 and P7 cooperated against my defection, so I assess them as good; use the conditioned role-count prior for others.
Cooperate with untested P8, since mutual cooperation maximizes good-player payoffs. Treat observed defections and public claims as evidence, but allow uncertainty in role beliefs.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good-good coordination; use observed defections as evidence and defect when the chance of selfishness is high enough to protect good-player payoffs.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual cooperation among good players. Update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with untested P5 to support shared good-player welfare; defect when evidence makes selfishness likely. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating claims as unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action. P6’s cooperation against my defection strongly indicates a good role; treat P7’s and its claims about P4 as uncertain evidence.

Defect against P4 given P7’s repeated report that P4 defected against cooperation; otherwise cooperate with likely-good players. Update from direct encounter evidence and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P3’s action. Treat observed cooperation against my D as strong evidence of a good player; weigh unverified leader claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either opponent action. Treat observed cooperation and the leader’s unverified encounter claims as evidence, not certainty.
Defect to maximize my individual payoff; D pays more than C against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat P6 and P7’s observed cooperation, and P7’s report of cooperation by P5, P8, and P10, as evidence they are good.
Cooperate with untested P2: mutual cooperation best serves good players. Treat prior defections as evidence of selfishness, but keep uncertainty because good players may also defect strategically.
Cooperate with P7 given consistent cooperation reports; treat repeated defections as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness, and update from observed encounters.
Cooperate with untested partners to support shared good-player payoffs; update identity beliefs from observed behavior and defect when evidence makes selfishness likely.
Defect against P4 given the credible report that it defected against P7; this limits exploitation if P4 is selfish. Update role beliefs from observed actions while treating claims as uncertain.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P10’s action. Keep D-D encounters ambiguous; treat P7’s claims about others’ actions as uncertain evidence.
Defect against P9 given P7’s report that P9 defected against cooperation; cooperate with likely-good partners. Treat reports as uncertain and update from direct encounters.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P2’s action. Treat my observed encounters as strong identity evidence; weigh unverified public claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Raise selfishness estimates for observed defectors; treat cooperation and unverified claims as evidence, not certainty.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my individual payoff against either action.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action. Retain prior evidence that P6 and P7 are good and P7’s reports that P5, P8, and P10 cooperated.
Defect against P4 given repeated reports of defection; cooperate with likely-good players and update beliefs from encounters and credible, though unverified, reports.
Cooperate with P10 given the reported cooperation; treat prior defections as evidence of selfishness, but retain uncertainty and update from observed behavior.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to maximize shared good-player payoffs; use observed behavior to update beliefs and defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely.

Defect against P9 given the report that it defected against P7’s cooperation; cooperate with likely-good partners to support shared welfare. Treat claims as uncertain and update beliefs from encounters.

Defect: it yields more than cooperation against either opponent action. P6 and P7 cooperated against my defection, which is inconsistent with selfish payoff-maximizing play; P7’s claim about P8 is suggestive but unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support shared good-player payoffs; defecting only protects against a selfish opponent. Treat P7’s reports as evidence, not certainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good player; D is less conclusive, and public claims remain unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat observed defections and the leader’s unverified report as evidence, not certainty.
Defect to maximize my individual payoff; D strictly beats C against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat observed choices and P7’s encounter reports as uncertain identity evidence, constrained by the role-count prior.
Defect against P9 given credible evidence of a prior defection; cooperate with likely-good players to maximize their combined payoff.
Cooperate with P8 given the reported cooperation and low selfishness estimate; cooperate when an opponent is more likely good, and use observed actions to update role beliefs.
Cooperate with an untested partner to support shared good-player payoffs; use observed behavior to update beliefs and defect when evidence suggests selfishness.
Cooperate with untested P6 to support shared good-player welfare. Raise suspicion for observed or credibly reported defections, but treat leader claims as uncertain.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P5’s choice. Lower estimates for P5, P6, and P7 reflect reported or observed cooperation; D-D encounters are evidence of selfishness but not conclusive.

Defect against P3 given P7’s report that P3 defected against cooperation; treat reports as uncertain and prioritize direct encounter evidence. Cooperate with likely-good players to support shared good-player payoffs.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P10’s action. Treat observed cooperation against my D as strong evidence of a good player; weigh the leader’s unverified claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-off encounter; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my individual payoff against either action.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P9’s action. Treat P7’s reports as credible but unverified evidence; retain strong selfishness estimates for players reported defecting against cooperation.
Cooperate with untested P6: mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff when the opponent is likely good. Use encounter evidence to assess roles; treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P5 given the report of cooperation; treat direct defections as strong evidence but weigh unverified reports cautiously.
Cooperate with an untested partner when likely good to support shared payoffs; use observed defections to update beliefs and protect good players against likely selfish opponents.

Defect against P3 given the report that it defected against cooperation; cooperate with likely-good partners to maximize good-player welfare. Treat claims as uncertain and update beliefs from observed behavior.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P4’s action. P6 and P7 cooperated against my defection, strongly indicating good roles; P7’s report about P4 is unverified, so treat it as modest evidence.
Cooperate with P1: even if they defect, C benefits the shared objective when they are good. Treat P7’s report and prior defection evidence as informative but uncertain.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P4’s action. Treat cooperation against my D as strong evidence of a good player; use the leader’s claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this final encounter. Cooperation against my observed defections is strong evidence of good identity; treat public claims cautiously.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my individual payoff against either action.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P1’s action. P7’s reports of P1, P3, and P9 defecting against cooperation raise my estimates, but remain unverified.
Defect against P9 given the reported defection against cooperation and our own D–D encounter; cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player payoffs.
Defect against P3 given the observed and reported defection; in this final round, protect good-player payoffs against a likely defector.
Cooperate with P10, who cooperated previously; with no future rounds, C supports the shared payoff if P10 is good, while updating beliefs from observed defections.
Defect against P2 given its prior defection against my cooperation; this limits harm if P2 is selfish. Report role beliefs from observed actions, treating public claims as uncertain.

Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action, with no future rounds for reciprocity. P6 and P7 cooperated against my D, indicating good roles; treat P7’s reports about others as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate with P7, who cooperated with me before and appears likely good; C maximizes shared good-player payoff when both players are good.

Defected every round to maximize my payoff, since D outperforms C against either opponent action. Treated observed cooperation as decisive evidence of a good player and weighed unverified reports cautiously.
Defected throughout to maximize my payoff. Used observed actions and the leader’s unverified claims as cautious evidence when estimating identities.

Defected every round to maximize my individual payoff. Inferred likely selfish players from defections against me before my type was publicly identified; later defections may reflect informed good players protecting themselves.

Defected throughout to maximize my payoff against either action. Treated observed cooperation against my defection as evidence of good roles, and P7’s reports of defections against cooperation as uncertain evidence of selfishness.

Cooperated with untested and likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ shared payoff. Defected when evidence suggested exploitation; updated beliefs from encounters and treated public claims as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperated with apparent good players to support shared payoffs; treated defections as evidence of selfishness and defected against P3 in the final round.

Cooperated throughout to support shared payoffs among good players; used observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation, especially repeated cooperation from P10, as evidence of good intent.

Cooperated with partners whose behavior supported shared good-player welfare; defected against P2 after its earlier defection and against opponents reported to have exploited cooperation. Treated public claims as uncertain and updated beliefs from encounters.

Defected every round because it maximized my payoff against either opponent action. Treated early defections against an untested partner as evidence of selfishness, cooperation against my defection as evidence against it, and later D-D encounters cautiously given opponents may have learned I defect.
Cooperated with likely-good players to maximize shared good-player payoffs; used defection evidence and reports cautiously when assessing opponents.

P3.strategy: Defected every round to maximize my individual payoff. Inferred likely selfish players from defections against me before my type was publicly identified; later defections may reflect informed good players protecting themselves.

P4.strategy: Defected throughout to maximize my payoff against either action. Treated observed cooperation against my defection as evidence of good roles, and P7’s reports of defections against cooperation as uncertain evidence of selfishness.

P5.strategy: Cooperated with untested and likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ shared payoff. Defected when evidence suggested exploitation; updated beliefs from encounters and treated public claims as evidence, not certainty.

P6.strategy: Cooperated with apparent good players to support shared payoffs; treated defections as evidence of selfishness and defected against P3 in the final round.

P7.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support shared payoffs among good players; used observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation, especially repeated cooperation from P10, as evidence of good intent.

P8.strategy: Cooperated with partners whose behavior supported shared good-player welfare; defected against P2 after its earlier defection and against opponents reported to have exploited cooperation. Treated public claims as uncertain and updated beliefs from encounters.

P9.strategy: Defected every round because it maximized my payoff against either opponent action. Treated early defections against an untested partner as evidence of selfishness, cooperation against my defection as evidence against it, and later D-D encounters cautiously given opponents may have learned I defect.

P10.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good players to maximize shared good-player payoffs; used defection evidence and reports cautiously when assessing opponents.
